decisive_items: 20% weight loss (12 kg) over one year
a lactate dehydrogenase level of 643 U/L
mesenteric lymph nodes measuring up to 27 mm but no distant metastases
response.rationale: HIV-positive patient with B symptoms, markedly elevated LDH, bulky mass, and lymphadenopathy strongly suggests lymphoma, especially HIV-associated DLBCL. Recurrent cervical cancer is plausible given prior history but lacks supporting tumor markers or gynecologic symptoms.

rejected.why: Sarcoma less likely without specific imaging or histologic features; elevated LDH is nonspecific.
Cecal cancer would typically involve mucosal symptoms and tumor markers; mass origin from vaginal wall favors other etiology.
Vaginal cancer alone does not explain systemic B symptoms and high LDH as well as lymphoma.
IBD would not produce a 15 cm mass with fistulous connection and high LDH without more typical GI symptoms.
Possible but less likely given negative tumor markers and no gynecologic complaints; lymphoma better fits systemic profile.
Carcinomatosis implies diffuse peritoneal spread, but imaging shows no distant metastases and mass is localized.
Carcinoma is too broad and contradicted by negative tumor markers and no distant metastases.
